ui.title: Garmin Connect MCP
ui.not_connected: Not connected yet. Log in once – your password is not stored, only the access tokens Garmin issues (valid for about six months). Two-factor authentication is supported: if it is enabled, you will be asked for the code.
ui.logout_confirm: Log out and delete the stored Garmin tokens?
ui.mfa_hint: Garmin has sent you a security code. Enter it here.
ui.state_failed: Garmin login failed – please log in again
ui.wa_create_only: create, but never delete or overwrite
ui.no_public_url: Set “Public address” in the configuration to see the full address. Until then, replace the domain placeholder.
ui.internal_url: Target for your tunnel / reverse proxy
ui.internal_hint: Point a public HTTPS hostname (e.g. in the Cloudflared app) at this address. Never publish port 8100 without HTTPS.
ui.secret_warning: Anyone who knows this URL can use your Garmin account through the AI tools. Treat it like a password.
ui.rotate_confirm: Generate a new secret URL? The old one stops working immediately and you must update your connectors.
ui.steps: Add it in your AI app as a custom connector / remote MCP server (no authentication). Details: see the Documentation tab.
ui.err_mfa: The security code was wrong or has expired.
ui.err_mfa_expired: The login took too long. Please start again.
ui.err_rate_limit: Garmin is rate-limiting logins. Please wait a few minutes and try again.
ui.err_connection: Garmin Connect could not be reached or rejected the login.
ui.err_csrf: The page was outdated. Please try again.
ui.err_too_many_attempts: Too many login attempts. Please wait 15 minutes – this protects your Garmin account from being locked.
ui.ok_rotate: New secret URL generated. Update your connectors.
ui.upload_hint: To let the AI create workouts on your watch, Garmin needs your consent to data uploads (required for EU accounts): Garmin Connect → Settings → Privacy settings → Data → “Upload device data” must be on. If your watch already syncs to Garmin Connect, this is usually already the case.
ui.oauth_hint: If you also use the ha-mcp app with its webhook proxy, your AI app may ask you to log in to your Home Assistant and grant access when adding the connector. That comes from ha-mcp and is harmless – just confirm it.
ui.login_wait: Logging in to Garmin – this can take up to 30 seconds. Please don't click again.
ui.reset_confirm: Discard your selection and use the areas and write access from the configuration again?
ui.tools_intro: Tick what the AI may use. ⓘ explains each tool. Saving restarts the server; afterwards your AI app may need a moment to see the new tool list.
ui.info_kind_read: Only reads data from Garmin Connect.
ui.info_kind_create: Adds something new to Garmin Connect (e.g. a workout or an entry), never deletes or overwrites.
ui.info_kind_change: Changes, overwrites or deletes existing data – or saves files. Allow deliberately.
ui.ok_tools: Selection saved. The server is restarting.
ui.ok_tools_reset: Selection reset – the configuration applies again.
ui.cleaned_up: Remote access is set to “direct”: the helper integration for the webhook was removed from Home Assistant. No restart needed.
ui.new_tools_hint: {n} new tools since you saved your selection – they are switched off.
ui.unknown_tools: These tool names in the configuration do not exist and are ignored (typo?):
ui.public_url_http: The public address uses http://. Most AI apps only accept https:// connectors.
ui.public_url_invalid: The “Public address” in the configuration is not a valid web address and is ignored. Example: https://home.example.com
ui.new_tools_banner: An update added {n} new tools (marked “new”). They stay switched off until you tick them and save.
ui.test_intro: Checks the server, your Garmin login and the connector URL from the internet – exactly the way your AI app reaches it.
ui.test_public: Connector URL reachable from the internet
ui.detail_not_logged_in: not logged in – log in above
ui.detail_relogin: login no longer valid – log out and log in again
ui.detail_no_public: public address unknown – set “Public address” in the configuration
ui.remote_active: Active – via your Home Assistant address
ui.remote_restart_needed: Home Assistant must be restarted once
ui.restart_hint: The app has installed or updated its small helper integration for remote access. Home Assistant loads it only after a restart: Settings → System → Restart (or the repair notice, if shown). Until then the connector cannot work – logging in to Garmin already works.
ui.no_base_url: Home Assistant has no external URL configured. Set it under Settings → System → Network, or enter it as “Public address” in the app configuration – until then, replace the placeholder.
ui.detail_no_config_access: no access to the Home Assistant config folder
ui.docs_table_head: | Tool | What it does | Type | Areas |
ui.detail_blocked_proxy: Cloudflare answered with HTTP {value} – its bot protection or a firewall rule blocks this test before it reaches Home Assistant. If your AI app works, ignore this. Otherwise allow the path /api/webhook/garmin_mcp_* in Cloudflare (Security → WAF / Bots).
ui.detail_http_forbidden: HTTP {value} – blocked before reaching the app (firewall, reverse proxy or IP allow list). If your AI app works, you can ignore this.
ui.relogin_needed: Garmin no longer accepts this login (e.g. after a password change). Log in again – your settings and the connector URL stay the same.
